problem_statement: An IPv4 header that carries options (Internet Header Length greater than the minimum, i.e. a header longer than the standard 20 bytes) is mishandled. The header's well-formedness check and the header length are not derived from the IHL field, so option-bearing packets are not validated correctly and downstream processing (e.g. NAT64 translation) computes header offsets from a fixed header size rather than the IHL-derived length, causing misread payload/ports. In addition, source-route options (loose/strict source and record route) present in the IPv4 header are not detected and discarded, so such packets should be rejected instead of translated. The behavior required is that header validity and header length reflect the IHL field, and that packets carrying source-route options are dropped.
